rows: What makes a porphyry Cu deposit form?
Exsolution of magmatic fluid from crystallizing subduction-related magma; Cu and Mo partitioned into the fluid; deposition at depth ~3-5 km via pressure drop
What is the zonation sequence in a porphyry system?
Core: potassic (K-feldspar+biotite+Cu-Mo veins); Phyllic (sericite+pyrite); Argillic (kaolinite); Propylitic (chlorite+epidote) — T decreases outward
Why does gold precipitate in epithermal systems?
Boiling: CO₂ loss raises pH → gold bisulfide complex Au(HS)₂⁻ destabilizes → native gold precipitates
Volcanogenic Massive Sulfide — seafloor deposit from hydrothermal venting; Cu-Zn-Fe-Au-Ag in sulfide minerals (pyrite, chalcopyrite, sphalerite)
How do fluid inclusions constrain ore formation conditions?
Trapping temperature (homogenization) and salinity (ice melting point) reveal fluid T, P, and composition at time of mineral growth
What does Δ³³S (sulfur MIF) tell you?
Mass-independent sulfur fractionation; non-zero Δ³³S in Archean rocks proves O₂-free atmosphere (UV photolysis of SO₂); records Great Oxidation Event timing
How do Pb isotopes fingerprint ore deposits?
Galena has no U or Th → Pb isotopes record the source of Pb at time of ore formation; correlates ore districts to basement rock type/age
What drives Mississippi Valley-Type deposit formation?
Basin-expelled hot saline brine mixing with H₂S (from sulfate reduction or bacterial) in carbonate platform rocks; no volcanic association
